page: The Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-amd is a compute-aligned virtual machine within Vultr's High Performance family. It runs on AMD EPYC x86_64 processors configured with 12 shared virtual CPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system provides 24.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. Storage is provisioned via a bundled 500 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without integrated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark assessments show solid execution for parallel tasks alongside distinct single-thread limitations. The instance reached a multi-core Geekbench score of 6387.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 27275.02, while single-core Geekbench recorded 1059.0 and single-threaded gzip compression registered in the lower bracket at 18.92 GB/sec. Memory profiling yielded a PassMark memory score of 1623.4 alongside uncached large-block read speeds of 79.14 GB/sec and write speeds of 44.07 GB/sec. The shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GHz clock frequency restrict raw single-threaded throughput, though multi-threaded compilation and image processing deliver stable median performance.

Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the density of 12 virtual cores paired directly with high-speed local NVMe storage, making it cost-effective for multi-threaded batch operations rather than single-core frequency-bound applications. Static web serving throughput reached 7.88 GB/sec, while in-memory operations demonstrated 11.99 million Redis SET operations per second. Consequently, this server is suitable for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, web application tiers, caching layers, and distributed database nodes that leverage local NVMe storage without requiring extensive memory overhead.

It operates without discrete GPUs and includes a single public IPv4 address. Benchmarks demonstrate solid multi-threaded performance, recording a multi-core Geekbench score of 6387.0, PassMark CPU score of 17153.85, and 11.99 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded metrics show limitations, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1059.0 and lower single-thread compression speeds. With its 1:2 memory-to-CPU ratio and fast local NVMe capacity, this instance offers efficient resource utilization for multi-threaded build jobs, web serving layers, caching clusters, and mid-tier database workloads requiring balanced parallelism over extreme single-core performance.
